## Summary

AC-8 of VTID-04223 (engineering memory for the agent executor) was the last
uncovered acceptance criterion: `buildAgentRecallQuery()` — the text
`dev_agent_memory` recall is embedded against at run start — had only an
incidental two-line assertion inside the larger
`vtid-04223-agent-memory-context.test.ts` suite, which does not pin the
absent-failure case at all.

Execution id: **a08daafd** (`dev-autopilot/a08daafd`).

## Change

Added ONE new test file, `services/gateway/test/vtid-04223-agent-recall-query.test.ts`
(test-only; no source edits). It reads the exported contract of
`buildAgentRecallQuery(input: { vtid, planMarkdown, priorFailure? })` and pins:

- **carries the VTID + the plan's first heading** — line 0 is exactly the VTID,
  line 1 contains the plan's `# …` heading, and the whole query is two lines
  because the plan is whitespace-collapsed into one (`\s+` → `' '`).
- **appends the prior failure when present** — a third line, verbatim.
- **omits it when absent** — `undefined`, `null`, `''` and whitespace-only all
  produce a byte-identical query to the no-failure call, with no trailing
  blank part to dilute the embedding.
- **bounds the plan clip** — 5,000 chars of plan yields a second line of
  exactly `AGENT_RECALL_QUERY_MAX_CHARS + 1` (the cap plus `…`), and the query
  is `${vtid}\n${clippedPlan}`.

Reading taken where the request left room: "the plan's first heading" is
pinned as *the plan text as passed in* (autopilot plans are a title line plus
body, and the function collapses the newlines itself), rather than by
re-implementing markdown heading extraction inside the test — the function has
no heading parser and inventing one would have asserted behaviour the source
does not have. `priorFailure` is treated as absent for whitespace-only input
too, since the request says "when present" and a trimmed empty string is not.

The suite mocks `dev-autopilot-execute` and `dev-agent-memory` (the two
network clients this module imports) so it stays a pure unit test of the pure
renderer, matching the mocking style of the sibling
`vtid-04223-agent-memory-context.test.ts`.

## Tests

- `jest services/gateway/test/vtid-04223-agent-recall-query.test.ts` → **1 suite, 4 tests, all pass**.
- `jest services/gateway/test/vtid-04223-agent-memory-context.test.ts` (regression: the existing suite that already asserts on this function) → **1 suite, 16 tests, all pass**.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `services/gateway` → **clean**.

No source file, no fixture and no config was modified, so no other suite in
the repo is affected.
